title: Examining the Impact of Data and Training Methods on Emergent and Subliminal Misalignment
abstract: arXiv:2605.12798v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Post-training a language model can induce surprising behavioral changes far beyond the intended training target. We study two particularly striking examples: emergent misalignment (EM), where fine-tuning on a narrow dataset leads to misaligned behavior in unrelated contexts, and subliminal learning (SL), where a student model inherits a teacher's misalignment through seemingly benign training data. We examine how the training data, evaluation data, and training method shape where and how strongly misalignment transfers between data and models. We characterize the data by the domain of a prompt (its topical context) and its task (the function the model performs), and we build natural-language and synthetic datasets organized as domain-task grids. translated_abstract: 对语言模型进行后训练可能引发远超预期训练目标的惊人行为变化。我们研究了两个尤为显著的例子：涌现性失对齐（EM），即在狭窄数据集上进行微调会导致模型在无关情境中表现出失对齐行为；以及阈下学习（SL），即学生模型通过看似无害的训练数据继承教师模型的失对齐特性。我们考察了训练数据、评估数据和训练方法如何决定失对齐在数据与模型之间于何处转移以及转移的强度。我们用提示词的领域（其主题语境）和任务（模型所执行的功能）来刻画数据，并构建了按“领域-任务”网格组织的自然语言数据集与合成数据集。我们发现，与共享微调数据领域的提示词相比，EM 更多地转移到与微调数据共享相同任务的提示词上。在合成环境中，模型已……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文通过构建按“领域-任务”网格组织的数据集，系统研究了训练数据、评估数据与训练方法如何影响涌现性失对齐（EM）与阈下学习（SL）中失对齐的转移，并发现 EM 主要沿任务而非领域进行转移。
en_tdlr: By constructing datasets organized as domain-task grids, this paper systematically examines how training data, evaluation data, and training methods shape the transfer of emergent misalignment (EM) and subliminal learning (SL), finding that EM transfers along tasks rather than domains.
